summary: Dynamic rate-limiter causing sustained 429s for ephemeral worker pool after cross-region clock skew
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden sustained 429 wave across a set of ephemeral worker processes immediately after a cross-region NTP adjustment. Horizon Analytics runs a dedicated pool in us-west with traffic mirrored to eu-west for redundancy. After a routine maintenance window that included an NTP re-sync on their fleet (~2026-03-12 04:10 UTC), their ingest orchestrator observed repeated 429s from Redwood API for ~18 minutes, even though token buckets appeared to have available credits in monitoring dashboards.

Impact:
- Affects their critical ingest pipeline for metrics enrichment; ~25% of webhook callbacks were rejected by Redwood for the duration.
- Customer-facing latency/backpressure caused retries and duplicated messages upstream.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-42), prod-us-west primary, geo-mirror eu-west.
- Ephemeral worker orchestrator that spins short-lived credentials per container (lifetime ~45s).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a burst of short-lived ephemeral workers (parallelism ~120) that each exchange for ephemeral API tokens.
2) Simultaneously run an NTP re-sync on the host fleet so local clocks jump by ~2.3 seconds.
3) Observe 429s from API starting within 30–60s of clock change and lasting ~18 minutes.

Observed logs (customer):
- Several hundred 429 responses with header X-RateLimit-Reason: token_window_mismatch.
- Metrics show token refill events out-of-sync between edge and origin (refill timestamps misaligned).
- No increase in error 5xx; only rejections.

Relevant notes:
- Customer believes short token TTL and concurrent credential churn amplify the issue.
- They attempted to stagger token refresh by 5s and saw the window of failures reduce but not fully disappear.

Requested outcome:
- Explanation of how clock skew interacts with token-windowed refill.
- Guidance on rate-limit configuration (burst pools/refill alignment) for ephemeral-heavy workloads on Dedicated pools.
- Short-term mitigation we can apply from our side while they adjust orchestration.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Support: reproduced pattern in internal canary with simulated 2s clock jump and ephemeral token lifetime of 30s. Hypothesis: edge proxies compute token-window buckets based on local time; small clock deltas cause origin and edge refill offsets. When ephemeral credentials are short-lived and many workers refresh simultaneously, the refills appear as multiple sub-windows from the origin while the edge still attributes counts to the previous window, leading to temporary double-accounting and early rejects.

SRE findings (first pass):
- Ingress proxy advertises refill epoch in X-RateRefill header; origin uses epoch from its local clock. If clocks differ by >1s at scale, token bookkeeping windows can be misaligned long enough to exhaust the perceived bucket.
- Monitoring shows refill counters synchronized again after origin-edge re-sync (~18 minutes), possibly due to smoothing/backoff in refill reconciliation logic.
- No evidence of a buggy refill loop; behaviour consistent with timing mismatch under high churn.

Immediate mitigations executed:
- Temporarily increased burst_delta for customer-dedicated-42 by +30% to allow a wider burst window while they stagger token refresh. (Change rolled at 2026-03-13 11:20 UTC)
- Added short-term telemetry to capture X-RateRefill versus origin refill times for future incidents.

Next steps suggested:
1) Recommend customer increase ephemeral token TTL to >=120s, or introduce jittered refresh staggering.
2) On Redwood side, implement a short-term tolerance of +/-3s between edge and origin refill epoch matching for dedicated pools (team: rate-limiter).
3) Add a healthcheck to detect repeated epoch mismatch and surface a self-heal (automatic smoothing) before rejects escalate.
comments: 2026-03-12 16:02 UTC - Maya Thompson (Support): Ticket opened after receiving incident report from Horizon Analytics. Assigned to on-call SRE. Attached customer logs and monitoring screenshots.

2026-03-12 18:10 UTC - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Reproduced locally with simulated clock jump. Filing hypothesis in investigation_notes. Will propose temporary burst_delta increase to reduce customer impact.
2026-03-13 11:25 UTC - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Increased burst_delta for dedicated pool customer-dedicated-42. Customer reports visible reduction in 429s during follow-up run. Continuing to monitor.

2026-03-13 13:40 UTC - Horizon Analytics (Customer): We applied a 5s jitter to token refresh and extended TTL to 90s; failures dropped substantially. Appreciate the burst_delta change. Would like recommendation for long-term config for dedicated pools.
2026-03-14 09:05 UTC - Maya Thompson (Support): Preparing formal guidance and scheduling a joint runbook review with Horizon and rate-limiter team next week.
resolution: Mitigation applied: temporary burst window widened on the customer's dedicated pool and additional telemetry enabled. Customer implemented jitter + longer TTL and reported immediate improvement. Long-term fixes recommended: increase tolerance for refill-epoch mismatch in rate-limiter, add epoch-mismatch health alert, and document recommended TTL/jitter settings for ephemeral-heavy workloads in Dedicated. Pending engineering RFC and scheduled follow-up with customer to close after next coordinated test.
